chunks: I do long that Allāh may cause separation between me and you,
and give me those who have a better right to be with me than you.
By Allāh, they are people of blissful ideas, enduring wisdom and true speech. They keep aloof from revolt.
They trod forward on the path (of Allāh) and ran on the high-road.
Consequently, they achieved the everlasting next life and easeful honours.
ai.seo_question: Who are the people of sound judgment and patience that the speaker wishes to be with?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) contrasts the political and spiritual failings of his contemporaries with the exemplary qualities of the 'right-hand' companions, emphasizing their sound judgment (ray) and patience (hilm). This reflection serves as a critique of the Umayyad era's leadership while highlighting the Shia ideal of steadfastness in truth and avoidance of rebellion (bagh). The description underscores the theological importance of aligning with those who possess both intellectual clarity and moral fortitude in the face of societal turmoil.
